terms.definition: The mental-training exercise uses an I-am-the-kind-of-person statement to promote desired routines.

concepts.author_mechanism: Repeated statements are described as helping make a self-definition automatic.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: Repeating an affirmation does not guarantee behavioral change; avoid identity coercion.
concepts.application: Draft one behavior-linked self-description and test it with a small action.
concepts.common_misreading: Treating source anecdotes, metaphors or motivating advice as guaranteed medical or performance outcomes.
concepts.alternative_explanation: Task learning, environmental supports, health, chance and external constraints could contribute without a discrete automatic mechanism.
concepts.ethical_clinical_cautions: Repeating an affirmation does not guarantee behavioral change; avoid identity coercion.
concepts.substantive_paraphrase: The revised-edition discussion connects identity affirmation as a cue to action to the larger psycho-cybernetics framework. It presents the premise that the mental-training exercise uses an i-am-the-kind-of-person statement to promote desired routines. It develops this through repeated statements are described as helping make a self-definition automatic. As an illustration, it describes source mental training exercise at printed 279. This is an attributed source argument, not independent evidence of causation; important limitations: Repeating an affirmation does not guarantee behavioral change; avoid identity coercion.
concepts.source_specific_illustration: Source mental training exercise at printed 279.
concepts.chapter_argument_role: A chapter-specific step in the argument, anchored to a first-hand read page, not standalone proof.
concepts.evidence_assessment: Book statement verified in original PDF; empirical corroboration not undertaken.
